# SuperGrep

> Retrieval subagents for Claude Sonnet. `find`, `search` and `sql` run
> locally over an index in plain files inside the repo - no accounts, no API
> keys, no server. `explore` and `ask` run in the cloud over the same
> index's platform copy, when a database is configured. Keyword (BM25)
> search is live seconds after indexing starts, semantic and hybrid search
> unlock as vectors backfill, and SQL composes ranked search with GROUP BY
> so "which files have the most code about X" is one query. The package,
> the CLI and the MCP server are still named `code-context`.

SuperGrep is built on infino (https://github.com/infino-ai/infino), an
embedded retrieval engine; the same engine and index format also serve
logs, docs, and agent memory.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): what it is, quick start (npm install or one-command
  Claude Code setup via npx), measured results, tool surface, CLI
  reference, and configuration.

## Using it

- Install: `npm install -g @infino-ai/code-context` (bins `code-context`
  and `cx`), then `cx index` in a repo.
- Zero-install for Claude Code (recommended; `alwaysLoad` keeps the tools in
  view when many MCP servers are configured):
  `claude mcp add-json code-context -s user '{"command":"npx","args":["-y","@infino-ai/code-context","mcp"],"alwaysLoad":true}'`.
  A Claude Code plugin (`/plugin marketplace add infino-ai/code-context`) bakes the same config in.
  These ship the three local tools; the cloud tools are on the
  `feat/platform-backend` branch, built from source with `--db`.
- MCP tools (stdio), local: `find` (every line containing an exact string,
  cited path:line like grep -n; complete and unranked - the grep
  replacement), `search` (exact terms AND meaning, one ranked pass, hits
  carry chunk content with path:line ranges), `sql` (read-only SELECT/WITH
  over `chunks(path, start_line, end_line, lang, symbol, content)`, ranked
  search functions (bm25_search/hybrid_search) usable as table-valued
  relations so search composes with GROUP BY). Cloud, with `--db`: `ask`
  (one retrieval, returned as the rows found rather than as prose) and
  `explore` (a question that spans the repository, answered in writing with
  the facts and chain of queries behind it). No reindex tool: the server
  auto-syncs in the background as queries arrive, and a first query on a
  never-indexed repo builds the index inline and answers on the same call
  (keyword live in seconds, vectors backfilling); `CX_AUTO_INDEX=0` restores
  a strict "index it first" error. `find`, `search` and `sql` take an
  optional `path` (absolute repo root) so one server serves multiple local
  repos in a session; `ask` and `explore` are scoped to the one platform
  database the server was started with.
- CLI: `cx index` (incremental; `--full`, `--watch`), `cx find`,
  `cx search`, `cx sql`, `cx status`, `cx mcp`.

## Evidence

- [The numbers](README.md#the-numbers): real agent runs (claude-sonnet-4-6)
  on a repo the model has not memorized, 36 questions in five categories.
  Sonnet's own bill falls 70% against its own Explore subagents, 58% all-in
  once the cloud tools' cost is counted; against plain file tools, 2.4x. A
  blind judge finds the quality gap real: it holds pinpoint symbol lookup
  and known-file questions, and loses aggregation, comprehension and
  by-meaning to a model reading the files itself - stated in the README as
  a loss, not glossed over.
- [Embedder eval](docs/embedder-eval.md): how the local embedding model
  was chosen.

## Concepts, FAQ, limits

- [Code search for coding agents](docs/concepts/code-search-for-coding-agents.md):
  the crawl-vs-retrieve model, when an index saves tokens, and where a plain
  grep is still the right tool.
- [FAQ](docs/faq.md): what it is, when an agent should use it, the five-tool
  MCP surface, local-vs-platform guarantees, freshness.
- [Tradeoffs](docs/tradeoffs.md): honest limits - the quality gap against a
  model reading files itself, no structural code intelligence, no token win
  on pinpoint lookups, one-time vector cost.

## Operational notes

- The local index lives in `.infino/` in the repo root (added to your
  `.gitignore` automatically on first index): plain files you can copy or
  cache in CI. With `--db`, the same chunks also load into a platform
  database over HTTPS, authenticated by a bearer key that is never passed
  as a command-line argument.
- Staged readiness: the keyword index commits before the embedding model
  finishes downloading; a failed vector stage degrades to keyword-only
  search instead of failing the index.
- Incremental sync re-chunks and re-embeds only changed files (size/mtime
  prefilter, then content hash); an unchanged tree is a fast no-op, and
  every sync updates both copies when `--db` is set.
- Config via env: `CX_ROOT`, `CX_INDEX_DIR`, `CX_AUTO_INDEX`, `CX_AUTO_SYNC`,
  `CX_SYNC_INTERVAL_SECS`, `CX_NO_EMBED`, `CX_MAX_FILES`,
  `CX_MAX_FILE_BYTES`. Platform settings are command-line flags on
  `cx index` and `cx mcp` - see [the reference](docs/reference.md).
